confirmed: The previously documented Digital Tide / Nocturnal Editorial / Chromatic Ocean visual direction is incorrect.
The screenshot reference is neo-brutalist: visible grid, heavy ink outlines, hard offset shadows, high-contrast paper surfaces, editorial type and tactile press states.
The final style should remain modern, attractive to young adults and not become visually hostile or exhausting.
Green, blue or another color may be used as an accent rather than the entire interface palette.
The product should prefer a coherent ready-made UI library/style registry over inventing every visual primitive from scratch.

decisions.title: Soft editorial neo-brutalism as the visual foundation
decisions.decision: Use a softened Swiss-editorial neo-brutalist language: off-white graph paper, ink-black 2px outlines, 3-4px hard shadows, square or lightly cut corners, restrained cobalt-blue accent, large Chinese editorial serif moments and neutral sans UI text. Use neobrutalism.com/RetroUI's current shadcn registry as the primary component source, with neobrutalism.dev as an additional reference, rather than generic shadcn plus effect libraries.
decisions.rationale: This matches the provided reference and provides an existing, accessible, source-owned React/Next.js component system. Softening border weight, color count and card density keeps the style youthful and tactile without making a long interview tiring or confrontational.

decisions.title: Reject adjacent style libraries for the MVP foundation
decisions.decision: Do not use Memphis, Bauhaus, Y2K, claymorphism, glassmorphism or pure Swiss minimalism as the base system. Their useful traits may inform composition, but the implementation foundation remains editorial neo-brutalism.
decisions.rationale: Memphis and Y2K skew decorative or juvenile, Bauhaus is rigid and primary-color coded, clay/glass reduce clarity or age quickly, and pure Swiss minimalism lacks the tactile playful signature requested. Neo-brutalism best balances existing library coverage, youth appeal and product-form compatibility.
